name: Azure CLI
description: Protects against destructive Azure CLI operations like vm delete, \ storage account delete, and resource group delete

destructive_patterns.name: vm-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az vm delete permanently destroys virtual machines.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
vm delete permanently destroys Azure VMs:

- VM is deallocated and deleted
- OS disk deleted (unless --os-disk=detach)
- Data disks detached but not deleted
- Public IP released

Preserve disks: az vm delete --os-disk detach --data-disks detach

destructive_patterns.name: storage-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az storage account delete permanently destroys the storage account and all data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
storage account delete destroys entire storage account:

- ALL blobs, files, queues, tables deleted
- All containers and their contents gone
- Cannot be recovered without backups

List contents first: az storage container list --account-name NAME

destructive_patterns.name: blob-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az storage blob/container delete permanently removes data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
storage blob/container delete removes data:

- Blob delete removes individual blobs
- Container delete removes container and ALL blobs
- Soft delete may allow recovery if enabled

Check soft delete: az storage account show --name NAME --query blobServiceProperties

destructive_patterns.name: sql-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az sql server/db delete permanently destroys the database.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
sql server/db delete destroys databases:

- Server delete removes ALL databases on server
- Database delete removes specific database
- Point-in-time restore possible within retention period

Create backup: az sql db export --name DB --server SRV --storage-uri URI

destructive_patterns.name: group-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az group delete removes the entire resource group and ALL resources within it!
destructive_patterns.explanation:
group delete removes ENTIRE resource group:

- ALL resources in the group deleted
- VMs, storage, databases, networks - everything
- Cannot be undone
- --no-wait returns immediately (deletion continues)

This is one of the most destructive Azure commands!

destructive_patterns.name: aks-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az aks delete removes the entire AKS cluster.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
aks delete removes the entire Kubernetes cluster:

- All nodes and workloads terminated
- Persistent volumes may be deleted
- Load balancers and IPs released
- Node resource group also deleted

Backup workloads: kubectl get all -A -o yaml > backup.yaml

destructive_patterns.name: webapp-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az webapp delete removes the App Service.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
webapp delete removes App Service:

- Application code and configuration deleted
- Custom domain mappings removed
- SSL certificates may be deleted
- Deployment slots also deleted

Backup config: az webapp config show --name NAME -g RG

destructive_patterns.name: functionapp-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az functionapp delete removes the Azure Function App.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
functionapp delete removes Azure Functions:

- All functions and configuration deleted
- Triggers and bindings removed
- Function keys lost
- Associated storage may be affected

Export functions if not in version control.

destructive_patterns.name: cosmosdb-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az cosmosdb delete permanently destroys the Cosmos DB resource.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
cosmosdb delete destroys Cosmos DB resources:

- Account delete removes entire Cosmos DB account
- Database delete removes database and all containers
- Collection delete removes container and data

Enable point-in-time restore for recovery options.

destructive_patterns.name: keyvault-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az keyvault delete removes the Key Vault. Secrets may be unrecoverable.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
keyvault delete removes Key Vault:

- All secrets, keys, certificates deleted
- Soft delete allows recovery (if enabled)
- Purge protection prevents permanent deletion
- Vault name reserved for recovery period

Check protection: az keyvault show --name NAME --query properties.enablePurgeProtection

destructive_patterns.name: vnet-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az network vnet delete removes the virtual network.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
network vnet delete removes virtual network:

- Network must be empty (no subnets in use)
- Connected resources lose connectivity
- Peerings to other VNets broken
- Network security groups may remain

Check usage: az network vnet subnet list --vnet-name VNET -g RG

destructive_patterns.name: acr-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az acr delete removes the container registry and all images.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
acr delete removes entire container registry:

- ALL repositories and images deleted
- All tags and manifests gone
- Webhooks and replications removed
- Registry name becomes available to others

List repos: az acr repository list --name REGISTRY

destructive_patterns.name: acr-repository-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az acr repository delete permanently deletes the repository and its images.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
acr repository delete removes repository:

- All tags and images in repository deleted
- Running containers unaffected (cached)
- New pulls will fail

List tags: az acr repository show-tags --name REG --repository REPO

destructive_patterns.name: acr-repository-untag
destructive_patterns.description: az acr repository untag removes tags from images.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
acr repository untag removes image tags:

- Tag removed from manifest
- Image still exists if other tags reference it
- Untagged images may be garbage collected

Lower risk: manifests can be re-tagged if digest known.

destructive_patterns.name: keyvault-item-delete-or-purge
destructive_patterns.description: Key Vault item delete/purge (az keyvault <key|secret|certificate|storage> …) — purge bypasses soft-delete and is irreversible.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
keyvault delete/purge on a Key Vault sub-resource:

- delete: soft-delete (recoverable within retention window)
- purge: PERMANENT; cannot be recovered; bypasses retention
- Purging a KEK (Key-Encryption-Key) makes all data encrypted under it unrecoverable
- Applications/services bound to the item fail immediately

Restore soft-deleted items within retention: az keyvault <sub> recover --name NAME --vault-name VAULT

Check purge protection: az keyvault show --name VAULT --query properties.enablePurgeProtection

destructive_patterns.name: role-assignment-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az role assignment delete removes an RBAC binding — users/SPs lose permissions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
role assignment delete revokes an RBAC assignment:

- The target user / service principal / group loses the role's permissions
- Can cascade — CI/CD pipelines, workloads, operators lose access
- Re-adding via `az role assignment create` is possible if IDs are known

List bindings first: az role assignment list --assignee PRINCIPAL-ID

destructive_patterns.name: ad-sp-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az ad sp delete removes a service principal — workloads using it lose auth.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
ad sp delete removes an Azure AD service principal:

- All workloads authenticating via this SP lose access
- SP credentials (client secrets, certs) are invalidated
- Can soft-delete and restore within 30 days via Graph API
- Associated app registration is NOT deleted (requires `az ad app delete`)

Preview usages: az role assignment list --assignee SP-APP-ID

destructive_patterns.name: ad-app-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az ad app delete removes an Azure AD app registration — every service principal for it stops working.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
ad app delete removes the Azure AD application registration:

- All service principals derived from this app break
- OAuth grants to this app are invalidated
- Associated federated credentials are deleted
- Can restore within 30 days via Graph API soft-delete

Consider disabling instead: az ad app update --id APP-ID --set disabledByMicrosoftStatus=None

destructive_patterns.name: network-dns-zone-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az network dns zone delete removes an Azure DNS zone — domains stop resolving.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
network dns zone delete removes an Azure DNS zone:

- All record sets in the zone are deleted
- Domains delegated to this zone's nameservers stop resolving
- Production traffic goes dark
- No undelete

Export records first: az network dns record-set list -g RG -z ZONE -o json > zone-backup.json

destructive_patterns.name: monitor-log-profiles-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az monitor log-profiles delete removes a subscription activity-log export — compliance/forensics.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
monitor log-profiles delete stops exporting the Azure activity log:

- Historical entries at the destination (Storage/Event Hub) are preserved
- Future activity events stop flowing to the configured export
- Compliance audit (SOC2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) may require this profile

Each subscription only supports one log profile at a time.

destructive_patterns.name: cosmosdb-sql-container-delete
destructive_patterns.description: az cosmosdb <api> <db|container|keyspace> delete permanently destroys Cosmos DB data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
cosmosdb <api> delete destroys Cosmos DB SQL/Mongo/Cassandra/Gremlin/Table API resources:

- Container/keyspace deletion removes ALL documents/rows inside
- Point-in-time restore is only available if continuous backup is enabled
- Periodic backups can restore within retention, with a new account name

Enable continuous backup for safer recovery: az cosmosdb update --name ACCOUNT --resource-group RG  --backup-policy-type Continuous
